diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since the eigenvalues of $Z^TGZ$ are all positive \cite{horn2013matrix}, and using the fact that $Z^T=Z^{-1}$ we can reformulate this problem as follows:

issues.failure_explanation: After H=ZY with Z^T Z=I, the maximizer of Tr(Y^T Z^T G Z Y) is the top eigenvector of Z^T G Z, while the minimizer of Tr(Y^T Z^T G^{-1} Z Y) is the bottom eigenvector of Z^T G^{-1} Z. These coincide only if Z^T G^{-1} Z = (Z^T G Z)^{-1}, which the paper justifies via Z^T=Z^{-1}; that inversion identity is valid only for square invertible Z, but Z is n x (n-h+1), so the two matrices differ in general. Counterexample: G = [[2,1,1],[1,2,0],[1,0,4/3]] (positive definite) with the legitimate fairness matrix F=(1/2,1/2,-1)^T (groups V_1={1,2}, V_2={3}); for an orthonormal basis {z_1,z_2} of ker F^T, the top eigenvector of Z^T G Z is proportional to z_1+3.02 z_2, whereas the bottom eigenvector of Z^T G^{-1} Z is proportional to z_1+1.57 z_2. Hence SMW2 does not share SMW1's maximizer. The entire subsequent chain (augmented Lagrangian, SMW3, SMW3b, the mu->infinity SMW limit, the reformulation problem, and the Fair-SMW algorithm) therefore solves min Tr(H^T G^{-1} H) s.t. F^T H=0, not the advertised fair normalized-cut relaxation min Tr(H^T L_sym H) s.t. F^T H=0.

failure_location.quote: Notice that \eqref{SMW2} is equivalent to \eqref{SMW1} in the sense that the maximizer $H$ is the same.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair; at minimum a repair must re-derive the constrained eigenproblem using the correct dual (Z^T G Z)^{-1} = Z^{-1} G^{-1} Z^{-T} (equivalently, work directly with Z^T G Z or an orthogonal projector onto ker F^T as in the cited S-Fair-SC), because Z^T G^{-1} Z and (Z^T G Z)^{-1} are genuinely different matrices.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's central theoretical claim -- that Fair-SMW (SYM, RW, AFF variants) solves the fairness-constrained spectral relaxation of normalized cut -- is unsupported: the derived objective is a different constrained eigenproblem, and every downstream step of the derivation inherits the wrong objective.
issues.title: Claimed equivalence of the G and G^{-1} fairness-constrained eigenproblems is false
issues.why_classification: The root claim is simply false and no local edit repairs it: the correct dualization requires a different derivation architecture, and the advertised guarantee (a solution of the fair spectral relaxation) is not delivered by the method as derived, even though a runnable algorithm remains.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \min_{H} \left( \frac{1}{2}\text{Tr}(H^T G^{-1} H) - \frac{\mu}{2} \text{Tr}(H^T F F^T H) \right) = \min_{H} \frac{1}{2}\text{Tr}\left(H^T \left( G^{-1} - \mu F F^T \right) H \right)
&= G^{-1} H - F\Lambda - \mu F F^T H

issues.failure_explanation: For the constrained problem min (1/2)Tr(H^T G^{-1} H) s.t. F^T H=0, the augmented-Lagrangian penalty must be + (mu/2)||F^T H||_F^2; with the stated minus sign the term rewards violating the fairness constraint and the displayed function is not an augmented Lagrangian. Consequently the stated gradient G^{-1}H - F Lambda - mu F F^T H and the Lambda=0 subproblem both carry G^{-1} - mu F F^T, directly contradicting the plus sign in the paper's central equation SMW3. As written, the derivation does not produce SMW3.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Flip the penalty sign in the Lagrangian to + (mu/2)||F^T H||_F^2 and the corresponding signs in the gradient (G^{-1}H - F Lambda + mu F F^T H) and the block system ((G^{-1}+mu F F^T)H - F Lambda = 0); the Lambda=0 subproblem then coincides with SMW3 and every subsequent step (SMW3b, the SMW limit, the algorithm) is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The derivation of the central penalized problem SMW3 (and with it the SMW identity step and everything built on it) is invalid as written; a reader cannot verify the paper's key equation from the given argument.
issues.title: Augmented Lagrangian has a negative penalty and the derived subproblem contradicts SMW3
issues.why_classification: The correction is a forced, local sign repair that leaves SMW3 and all downstream content intact; no substantive claim, rate, or scope is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $D^{-1}$ is an invertible diagonal matrix, it is of full rank, and multiplying by it from the right does not change the row space $ \mathcal{R}(F^T D^{-1}) = \mathcal{R}(F^T) $ and the identity \eqref{eq:identity} holds.
The expression $F^T D^{-1} = F^T D^{-1} P_F$ holds true if and only if every row vector of $F^T D^{-1}$ is invariant under the projection $P_F$.

issues.failure_explanation: Right-multiplication by D^{-1} rescales the i-th entry of every row of F^T by 1/d_i; the row space is preserved only when the scaling is constant on each protected group, so the claimed identity holds only if degrees are constant within every group -- the paper's justification ('multiplying by it from the right does not change the row space') is false in general. Counterexample: n=4, V_1={1,2}, V_2={3,4}, degrees (1,2,1,1), F=(1/2,1/2,-1/2,-1/2)^T gives F^T D^{-1} = (1/2,1/4,-1/2,-1/2) but F^T D^{-1} F (F^T F)^{-1} F^T = (7/16,7/16,-7/16,-7/16). The identity then feeds the simplification P = I - F(F^T Wcal F)^{-1} F^T Wcal, the symmetry of Wcal P, and the similarity argument; with the identity false these steps collapse, so the claim that U_rw has real eigenvalues is unproven (the argument is valid only for graphs whose degrees are constant within each group).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either prove realness of the eigenvalues of U_rw by a correct argument (a new lemma, e.g. a valid symmetrization of D^{-1} Wcal P) or restrict the theorem to graphs whose degrees are constant within each protected group; both are contained but nontrivial repairs.
issues.overall_effect: The RW-Fair-SMW variant loses its only theoretical justification (a real spectrum for the nonsymmetric U_rw); the SYM and AFF variants retain theirs (thm:added-2, thm:added-3 and the symmetric argument).
issues.title: thm:added-5 proof relies on a false identity, leaving realness of the U_rw spectrum unproven
issues.why_classification: The proof fails at a concrete step and the key identity is demonstrably false, but the claim may still be true and the damage is confined to one variant's spectral guarantee; a contained new argument or an added hypothesis repairs it without global rearchitecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \State Construct the fairness-adjusted matrix $U_{\text{sym}} = G_{\mathrm{sym}} - M (F^T M)^{-1} F^T G_{\mathrm{sym}}$
(G^{-1}+\mu FF^T)^{-1} &\rightarrow G - GF (F^T GF)^{-1} F^T G\

issues.failure_explanation: The derivation fixes U = G - GF(F^T G F)^{-1} F^T G, which the algorithmic formula U = G - M(F^T M)^{-1} F^T G reproduces only when M = G F. The algorithm instead sets M = G_sym^{-1} F, yielding the different matrix G - G^{-1}F(F^T G^{-1}F)^{-1}F^T G; for symmetric G_sym this matrix is nonsymmetric (the derived U is symmetric), so 'top k eigenvectors corresponding to largest eigenvalues' is not even well-defined as stated, and the computed embedding differs from the paper's fairness-adjusted matrix. (G^{-1}F is also not a projection matrix, despite the step's name.)

failure_location.quote: \State Compute the projection matrix $M = G_{\mathrm{sym}}^{-1} F$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Set M = G_sym F (a one-token correction forced by the text's own definition U = G - GP); the remaining steps then compute the derived U_sym.
issues.overall_effect: As specified, Fair-SMW does not implement the paper's derived fairness-adjusted matrix; its output contract (top eigenvectors of U = G - GP) fails, independently of the separate dualization defect in the derivation.
issues.title: Fair-SMW algorithm builds U from M = G_sym^{-1}F instead of the derived M = G_sym F
issues.why_classification: The fix is short, local, and forced by the paper's own definition of U; it preserves the intended construction and all subsequent steps, so no substantive claim is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: A similar statement holds for $G_{\text{rw}}$ and $G_{\text{aff}}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury gives (G_sym + mu F F^T)^{-1} = G_sym^{-1} - G_sym^{-1} F (mu^{-1} I + F^T G_sym^{-1} F)^{-1} F^T G_sym^{-1}, not the displayed right-hand side; the displayed expression is the mu -> infinity limit of (G_sym^{-1} + mu F F^T)^{-1} used in the main text, so the proof's starting equality is wrong. The remaining chain is correct under A_sym F = 0, so the main identity U = [I - F(F^T F)^{-1} F^T] G_sym survives, but the closing claim that a similar statement holds for G_rw and G_aff does not follow: A_sym F = D^{-1/2} W D^{-1/2} F = 0 only gives D^{-1/2} F in ker W, whereas the analogous simplification of U_aff or U_rw requires W F = 0 (i.e. F in ker W), a strictly stronger condition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the first display with the limit expression U = G_sym - G_sym F(F^T G_sym F)^{-1} F^T G_sym and delete (or re-prove under appropriate hypotheses) the sentence 'A similar statement holds for G_rw and G_aff.'
issues.overall_effect: Auxiliary supporting result: the special-case identity is recoverable after correcting the first display, but the stated analogies for the RW and AFF variants are unsupported and generally false.
issues.title: thm:added-6 proof starts from a wrong expression for U and its generalization to G_rw and G_aff is unjustified
issues.why_classification: The main identity is correct under its hypothesis and only the proof's opening display plus an overbroad closing sentence need repair; the result is auxiliary and unused downstream.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For a weighted, undirected graph, the quadratic form of the unnormalized Laplacian, normalized by the degree matrix, is bounded by 2.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof establishes only the upper bound sup <= 2 (via (a-b)^2 <= 2(a^2+b^2)), but the displayed statement claims equality = 2 for every weighted undirected graph. Equality fails in general: for the triangle K_3, L_sym = I - A/2 has eigenvalues 0, 3/2, 3/2, so the supremum is 3/2 < 2; equality requires bipartite-type structure. The correct general statement is the inequality, which is all that downstream results (thm:added-2) actually use.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the displayed equality to sup <= 2; a one-symbol repair with no downstream effect.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem as stated is false for non-bipartite graphs; the bound itself, the only part used downstream, remains valid, so no dependent result fails.
issues.title: thm:added-7 asserts sup = 2 but proves only the bound <= 2, which fails to be equality for non-bipartite graphs
issues.why_classification: The argument is valid for the inequality and only the statement's equality overclaims; a one-symbol correction preserves every use of the result.
